subject: Materials Science
title: Hot Corrosion: Salt Plus Heat
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Hot Corrosion: Salt Plus Heat.

hook.text: A gas turbine ingests sea salt spray — at 900°C the salt melts and destroys the protective oxide scale.

buildup.text: Hot corrosion occurs when molten salt deposits dissolve the oxide layer that normally protects the metal.

discovery.text: Sodium sulfate from fuel sulfur and ingested salt is the main culprit — it melts around 884°C.

twist.text: Hot corrosion attacks fastest in a narrow temperature band where salts are molten — too hot and they evaporate.

climax.text: Naval gas turbines need special coatings and fuel specifications to survive salt-laden air.

punchline.text: A pinch of salt at the wrong temperature eats through superalloys.

quiz.question: What causes hot corrosion in gas turbines?
options: Molten salt deposits dissolving the protective oxide scale
Excessive fuel flow overheating the blades
